newsitem.title: UK: Bozell purchase offers True North clout in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Bozell purchase offers True North clout in Europe.

text.p: The acquisition on Thursday by True North Communications Inc of Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt (BJK&E) Inc advertising agency network will give True North important new clout in Europe, executives said on Friday.
True North, which is based in Chicago and owns Foote, Cone & Belding (FCB), the biggest ad agency in the United States, announced on Thursday it was buying New York-based BJK&E for $440 million.
True North, a holding company, said the merger created the world's sixth largest advertising company and meant True North now had two global ad agencies, FCB and Bozell Worldwide.

One senior advertising executive in London who asked not to be identified said the purchase was good news for True North because Bozell brought larger presence in Europe, digital interactive skills and other aspects of non-traditional advertising to the merged group.

He told Reuters the deal was good for Bozell because it brought True North's financial clout. "It's truly good news for both the clients and the staff of both agency groups. I can't see any downside and I can see a lot of upside," the executive said.

Advertising executives had been expecting True North to make a big acquisition in the last few months, after a 10-year-old global cooperation agreement with Publicis SA , a Paris-based group, was dissolved in the spring.

The break-up with Publicis basically left True North as an advertising holding company without a significant ad agency presence outside the U.S., since FCB, while a major player in its home market, lacks strong presence outside the U.S.

Bozell has expanded rapidly in Europe in the last two years by building up diversified communications skills that include Website technology, sponsorship, public relations and other services that go beyond traditional "above-the-line" advertising.

The Bozell group based in New York owns subsidiaries including Poppe Tyson, an agency that creates Websites for clients, Delaney Fletcher Bozell, a medium-sized ad agency in London, and the Charles Barker public relations firm.
"Bozell brings a lot to the party," the senior executive told Reuters. "What they (True North) bring to the party are a public quotation and financial resources," he said.

Martin Jones, the managing director of the Advertising Agency Register, a group in London that matches agencies with clients, said the acquisition would help True North break away from being too U.S.-focused.
"FCB is not very big over here (in Europe). They needed to bolster their presence outside the U.S.," he told Reuters.
"Culturally, American (ad) agencies and European agencies are so different...Delaney Fletcher Bozell has a very 'UK flavour'," Jones said.
He said American-based agencies were at a disadvantage to competitors outside the U.S. unless they had good local partners or otherwise established local credentials.

That's an important theme for international ad agencies, which have been scrambling in the last few years to globalise, in order to keep up with multinational clients that are trying to expand market share outside traditional markets in the U.S. or western Europe.
"People sometimes say the big U.S. agencies use a 'letterbox' approach, whereby they create one ad in the U.S. and then just drop it in different people's letterboxes around the world," Jones said.
That is not an approach that always works -- and sometimes it backfires -- because of cultural differences.
The senior advertising executive told Reuters the acquisition would give the two agency networks stronger media-buying clout, another important element in an increasingly competitive market.

Multinational clients want their ad agencies to provide strong global media-buying services -- the service whereby an agency or specialised company advises a client on where to run ads and then books the advertising space on behalf of the client.
